decisions.question: Is the product called UtilityHub or Juristic Platform, and which name appears in the UI header, LINE messages, the receipt letterhead and the document set? (merges Q-P-01)
decisions.decision: "Juristic Platform" is the single product name in English, used in every document title, the repo, the code, the login screen and the browser tab title. "UtilityHub" is deleted from the PRD and never used again. The Thai/English thesis titles in the PRD are unchanged. In the running app the top-left header shows the apartment name from Settings (demo seed: "ศุภาลัย เรสซิเดนซ์") with the system name "Juristic Platform" in 11px muted text underneath; the login page shows "Juristic Platform" as the H1 plus the Thai subtitle "ระบบจัดการค่าน้ำ ค่าไฟ และค่าส่วนกลาง". The receipt letterhead carries ONLY the apartment's own name, address, tax ID and phone from Settings — never the software name, because the receipt is issued by the juristic person, not by the software. LINE messages carry no product branding at all; where a signature is needed they are signed "— นิติบุคคล {apartment_name}" (one space after นิติบุคคล), because the tenant sees the apartment's Official Account, not a product.
decisions.rationale: The HTML template, the repo directory and every existing artifact already say Juristic Platform, so one edit in the PRD is cheaper than renaming everything else. Separating the software name from the letterhead is not cosmetic: a receipt headed with a software brand is not usable by the tenant.

decisions.question: Is the UI Thai-only, and how do the English page identifiers and the four bill statuses appear to users? (merges Q-P-16)
decisions.decision: Thai-only UI, no language switcher, no i18n framework — Thai strings are written directly in the templates. English survives only as identifiers in the database, routes, API payloads, test selectors and this documentation set. Fixed mapping, to be used verbatim everywhere. Statuses: Draft = ฉบับร่าง, Unpaid = รอชำระ, Paid = ชำระแล้ว, Overdue = เกินกำหนด. Pages: Login = เข้าสู่ระบบ, Dashboard = ภาพรวม, Rooms = ห้องพัก, Tenants = ผู้เช่า, Meter Reading = จดมิเตอร์, Monthly Billing = บิลประจำเดือน, Bill Detail = รายละเอียดบิล, Payment = รับชำระเงิน, Receipt = ใบเสร็จ, Announcements = ประกาศ, Reports = รายงาน, Settings = ตั้งค่า, Users = ผู้ใช้งานระบบ (D-46). Primary buttons: Approve & Send = อนุมัติและส่งบิล, Confirm Cash Payment = ยืนยันรับเงินสด, Print Receipt = พิมพ์ใบเสร็จ, Save = บันทึก. Every element that renders a status must carry a stable test hook data-status="Draft|Unpaid|Paid|Overdue" so tests assert on the English identifier while the human reads Thai.
decisions.rationale: Users are Thai; the English page names in the PRD are engineering identifiers, not user-facing copy. The data-status hook gives QA stable selectors for free and removes the only real argument for a bilingual UI.

decisions.question: What are the binding currency, number, date and timezone formats?
decisions.decision: Timezone Asia/Bangkok everywhere; the server sets TZ=Asia/Bangkok and MySQL time_zone='+07:00'; no UTC is ever shown to a user. Gregorian years only (2026), never Buddhist Era, in UI, LINE and receipt. Money: thousands separator, two decimals in tables, on Bill Detail and on the receipt (1,790.00); the unit is written "บาท" after the number in LINE messages and in sentence text (1,790 บาท) and trailing ".00" is dropped there. The ฿ glyph is permitted in this documentation set and in static mockups where space is tight; the running application and every LINE message write the number followed by "บาท", because the glyph renders inconsistently in the LINE client — this narrows the doc-set convention, it does not forbid it. Table money columns are right-aligned with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. Meter readings and units are integers with thousands separators (1,260 / 10 หน่วย). Room area is written 30 ตร.ม. Dates: UI lists and forms use d MMM yyyy Thai short (3 ก.ย. 2026); LINE messages and the receipt use full Thai month (3 กันยายน 2026); the database and every API payload use ISO 8601 (2026-09-03); the billing period key is YYYY-MM (2026-09) and is displayed as "กันยายน 2026". Time of day is 24-hour with the suffix น. (14:30 น.).
decisions.rationale: Three documents, three screens and one LINE template will otherwise each invent their own format. Fixing it once makes every example in the doc set and every test assertion copy-pasteable.

decisions.question: One building, several buildings, or multiple properties? (merges Q-P-17)
decisions.decision: Exactly one property and one building. Settings holds a single apartment profile (name, address, tax ID, phone, office hours, due day). Rooms are keyed by a room code that is a free VARCHAR(10) unique across the system — the seed uses plain numbers (205), but the column tolerates "A-205" so a future building prefix needs no migration. There is no building table, no building column, no building filter, and no property scoping in any query. Multi-building and multi-property are explicit non-goals recorded in the limitations list (D-05).
decisions.rationale: Matches the single ข้อมูลอพาร์ตเมนต์ section in PRD §12 and the 80-room Dashboard example. Reserving the room-code format costs nothing and keeps the door open without paying for it now.

decisions.question: What is the authoritative list of things the system deliberately does not do?
decisions.decision: The PRD §24 exclusions stand absolutely and must never be reintroduced in any document, mockup, test case or seed row: no rent, no lease contracts, no mobile app, no payment gateway, no cards, no online banking, no slip upload, no QR payment, no IoT or automatic meters, no AI/ML. In addition, these v1 limitations are decided here and must be listed verbatim in the Limitations section of every document that has one: (1) no proration for mid-period move-in/move-out (D-08); (2) no partial payment — a bill is paid in full or not at all (D-24); (3) no late fee, no interest, no penalty of any kind (D-21); (4) no refund, credit note or balance inside the system — a mis-keyed payment is voided and the cash is returned across the counter (D-25); (5) no multi-building support (D-04); (6) no VAT and no tax invoice — the receipt is a non-tax ใบเสร็จรับเงิน (D-27); (7) no tenant-facing web login — tenants only ever receive LINE messages; (8) no email or SMS channel; (9) the system cannot tell a delivered LINE message from one silently dropped because the tenant blocked the Official Account — LINE reports both as success (D-30); (10) receipt numbers are unique and monotonic but NOT gapless (D-26, D-27); (11) a receipt printed from the browser's own menu instead of the พิมพ์ใบเสร็จ button carries no สำเนา mark (D-27); (12) the LINE free plan's 500-message monthly allowance is displayed but never enforced — exhausting it silently stops delivery (D-34).
decisions.rationale: An out-of-scope list that lives in one PRD section gets quietly re-expanded by whichever document is written last. Naming the derived limitations here makes each one a decision someone would have to overturn, not an omission someone can fill in.

decisions.question: Where does the previous reading come from for the first period, a newly created room, or a re-occupied room? (merges Q-E-02, Q-U-08)
decisions.decision: Opening readings live on the room record, never in meter_readings. The Rooms create/edit form carries three mandatory fields written to rooms: baseline_water INT UNSIGNED (เลขมิเตอร์น้ำเริ่มต้น), baseline_electric INT UNSIGNED (เลขมิเตอร์ไฟเริ่มต้น) and one shared baseline_date DATE (วันที่เริ่มต้น). No synthetic reading row is ever written, so nothing can collide with the room's first real reading under UNIQUE(room_id, period, utility_type), no room is ever billed off a placeholder row, and no zero-usage flag fires on a new room. The previous-reading lookup (D-14) therefore has exactly one code path: the most recent earlier reading if one exists, otherwise the room's baseline for that utility with previous_period = 'baseline'. The Meter Reading screen always shows Previous as read-only text. Baselines are Admin-only and editable only while the room has no meter_readings row at all. A re-let room needs no baseline edit — its departing tenant's final reading is already the most recent earlier reading and D-14 finds it (D-08).
decisions.rationale: Two columns on rooms delete the entire class of first-period special cases without inventing a reading row that the unique key would later overwrite. This is the difference between billing 10 units and billing 1,260 units in month one — the most visible possible failure.

decisions.question: Are vacant rooms billed, in particular for the common area fee? (merges Q-P-11, Q-E-08, Q-U-09)
decisions.decision: Vacant rooms are skipped entirely by the billing run: no bill, no meter reading requirement, no common area fee, no owner invoice, no LINE recipient. A room is billable if and only if rooms.status = 'Occupied' AND it has exactly one tenant row with status = 'Active' on the generation date. Room status is derived from the tenant link and is not independently editable: linking an active tenant sets Occupied, ending the tenancy sets Vacant (D-08, D-10). Vacant rooms still appear on the Rooms page (badge ว่าง) and in the Dashboard room counts, and staff may still record readings for them voluntarily through the ห้องว่าง filter on the Meter Reading page (D-15) — those readings are stored and used as the previous value when the room is re-let, but never produce a bill.
decisions.rationale: This is the only reading consistent with the PRD §16 arithmetic (ค่าส่วนกลาง 70,350 = 2,010 sqm = 67 occupied rooms × 30 sqm, not 80 rooms) and it removes an entire class of bills that have no recipient, no payer and no LINE target.

decisions.question: Who is billed when a tenant moves in or out mid-period, and is anything prorated? (merges Q-P-10)
decisions.decision: No proration of any kind: the tenant whose tenancy is Active on the bill generation date receives the entire period's bill — full water, full electricity, full common area fee — and is the LINE recipient. Ending a tenancy is a settlement, not a status flip. The action สิ้นสุดสัญญาเช่า (Admin only) is BLOCKED unless (a) a final reading exists for both utilities for that room, dated on or after the last period the room was billed for, and (b) the bill covering that reading exists and is Paid. Order of operations, printed verbatim in the User Manual: record the final reading → run generation for that room, which creates its bill in the current period (D-18) → approve and send → take cash at the counter and issue the receipt → only then end the tenancy. The LINE binding is cleared at that last step and not before, so the departing tenant still receives both their final bill and their payment confirmation. Tenants carry วันที่เข้าอยู่ and วันที่ย้ายออก, shown on the Tenants page and in the per-room history, but neither date influences any amount. The outgoing tenant's bills, payments and receipts stay attached to that tenant forever and remain visible in the room's 12-month history (D-42). No consumption ever crosses a tenancy: the departing tenant's final reading is the incoming tenant's previous reading through the ordinary D-14 lookup, so nothing is re-entered and nothing is billed twice.
decisions.rationale: Proration plus off-cycle settlement bills roughly doubles the billing logic for a semester project, and prorating a common fee is lease-contract logic that PRD §24 puts out of scope. Gating the end of a tenancy on a settled final bill is what makes the office rule executable instead of aspirational — without it the departing tenant's last month is skipped by the run and silently charged to the next tenant.

decisions.question: If a room's area changes, does it rewrite bills and receipts already issued? (merges Q-P-12)
decisions.decision: No. At bill generation the bill row snapshots room_code, room_area_sqm and tenant_name_snapshot, and the common area bill item snapshots both the area and the rate used. Every screen, print view and LINE message renders these from the bill's own snapshot and never joins live to rooms or tenants. Changing a room's area therefore affects only bills generated afterwards. The guarantee is stated precisely: the BILLED DATA on a reprint — units, rates, area, tenant name, line amounts, total, receipt number, payment date — is identical forever; the page is not, because the letterhead is rendered live from Settings (D-01) and a reprint carries the สำเนา mark (D-27). No test asserts byte-identity. Area is DECIMAL(6,2), Admin only, and every change is audited (D-38). There is no versioned room-area table.
decisions.rationale: Three snapshot columns make reprints reproducible by construction. Effective-dated area versioning adds a table for an event that happens roughly once a year and can always be added later.

decisions.question: What exactly is a tenant record, how many per room, and who may create and end one?
decisions.decision: One room has at most one Active tenant at a time; a tenant record belongs to exactly one room. Fields: ชื่อ-นามสกุล (required), เบอร์โทรศัพท์ (required, Thai mobile format 0XXXXXXXXX validated), LINE User ID (read-only, filled only by the linking flow in D-29 — never typed by staff), ห้อง (required), วันที่เข้าอยู่ (required), วันที่ย้ายออก (nullable, not hand-editable), สถานะ (Active / Inactive). Status is SET BY AN ACTION, never derived from a date and never future-dated: สิ้นสุดสัญญาเช่า (D-08) sets status='Inactive', writes วันที่ย้ายออก = the date the action was taken, clears the LINE binding and sets rooms.status='Vacant' in the same transaction, so no scheduled job is needed and D-07's billable-room test always reads a settled value. Admin only may create, edit or end a tenancy; Staff cannot see the Tenants page at all (D-36). A tenant record is never deleted — bills, payments and receipts reference it. Re-letting a room creates a new tenant record even if the same person returns.
decisions.rationale: The PRD names the fields and nothing else; without the one-active-tenant rule the LINE recipient for a bill is ambiguous, and a status derived from a future date would silently change the billable-room set with nothing running to make it happen.

decisions.question: What exactly is a room record, where does the floor come from, and can a room be deleted?
decisions.decision: rooms holds: room_code VARCHAR(10) UNIQUE (D-04); floor TINYINT NOT NULL, entered on the form and NEVER parsed from the room code — D-15's floor grouping and D-35's floor audience both read this column, and a code like "A-205" cannot be parsed; room_type VARCHAR(20) nullable and display-only, which is where PRD §5's ประเภทห้อง lives — it is a label and never affects any amount; area_sqm DECIMAL(6,2), Admin only, audited (D-09, D-38); baseline_water, baseline_electric, baseline_date (D-06); status derived from the tenant link (D-07). A room is never deleted once any bill references it, because that would break D-09's reprint guarantee: the form offers ปิดใช้งานห้อง instead, which excludes the room from billing and from every list except an explicit ปิดใช้งาน filter. A room with no bills at all may be deleted outright.
decisions.rationale: Four other decisions consume fields that no decision created. Storing the floor instead of parsing it is one column against a class of bugs on the day someone types a lettered room code, and deactivation rather than deletion is the same guarantee D-10 already gives tenants.

decisions.question: What identifies a billing period, and is there an open/close state machine? (merges Q-P-06, Q-E-01, Q-U-01)
decisions.decision: A billing period is the BILLING month, a plain YYYY-MM string stored on meter_readings and bills — there is no periods table, no Admin "open period" action, no period lock and NO CLOSED STATE; the word "closed" appears in no document, screen or test. The office reads meters in the first days of month M and those readings, the bills and the due date all belong to period M; the consumption they cover is whatever accrued since the previous reading (D-14). The demo therefore reads on the 1st, period = that month, due on the 5th, paid on the 3rd, one receipt number — all four labels agree, which is only true under this definition. Bills carry UNIQUE(room_id, period). The Meter Reading and Monthly Billing pages have a month picker defaulting to the current calendar month in Asia/Bangkok. Data is protected not by a period state machine but by the bill status guard in D-12/D-22: a reading is editable exactly while its room's bill for that period is Draft or does not yet exist. Progress is shown, not stored: Monthly Billing renders one derived completeness line for the selected period — "บิลครบทุกห้อง {billed}/{billable} · อนุมัติแล้ว {approved} · ชำระแล้ว {paid}".
decisions.rationale: Billing-month periods are the only reading that reproduces the PRD §28 demo exactly. Dropping the open/close state machine removes a table, two Admin actions and a whole class of "period is closed" bugs, because the bill status already answers every question the lock would have answered — and a derived completeness line gives the operator the signal the lock was standing in for.

decisions.question: What is the shape of a reading row, when may it be edited, and by whom? (merges Q-E-05, Q-U-05)
decisions.decision: One row per room per period per utility: UNIQUE(room_id, period, utility_type) where utility_type is 'water' or 'electric'. The row stores previous_reading, current_reading and units as a snapshot computed at save time, plus previous_period (the period the previous value came from, or 'baseline'), recorded_by, recorded_at. A double-submitted save is an UPSERT on the unique key, so it is harmless — the lookup in D-14 excludes the row being written by construction, so a re-save can never take itself as its own previous. Because previous_reading is a snapshot, editing an old month's reading would leave the NEXT month's previous_reading stale; that is exactly why D-22 permits reverting only a room's most recent bill, which is the one guard that keeps the chain intact. Edit rights: Staff and Admin may create and edit a reading while the room's bill for that period is Draft or absent; saving recalculates that Draft bill in place immediately (D-18). Once the bill is approved (Unpaid/Paid, or displaying as Overdue) the reading is frozen for everyone — the only way back is Admin reverting the bill to Draft (D-22). The Meter Reading form shows the frozen state as read-only fields with the note "บิลอนุมัติแล้ว แก้ไขไม่ได้".
decisions.rationale: The unique key makes double-submit a non-event and the snapshot makes a printed bill reproducible — but a snapshot chain is only safe if nothing upstream of an approved bill can move, which is why the edit window and the revert window are the same window.

decisions.question: What happens when the current reading is below the previous one, and are implausible-but-valid readings flagged? (merges Q-P-14, Q-E-03, Q-U-03)
decisions.decision: Hard block, plus one explicit replacement path, plus two soft flags. (1) Hard block, applied ONLY when the meter-replacement checkbox is off: if current_reading < previous_reading the Save button is disabled and the inline Thai error "เลขมิเตอร์ปัจจุบันน้อยกว่าเดือนก่อน ({previous_reading}) กรุณาตรวจสอบ" is shown; the API rejects it with 422 for every role. units can never be negative — a database CHECK as well as a form rule. (2) Meter replacement, available to BOTH roles because staff are the ones standing at the meter: the checkbox "เปลี่ยนมิเตอร์ในรอบนี้" reveals two integer fields, เลขสุดท้ายของมิเตอร์เดิม (old_final) and เลขเริ่มต้นของมิเตอร์ใหม่ (new_start, defaults to 0), plus a required Thai reason. With the box ticked the current-below-previous block does not apply; the validation is instead old_final ≥ previous_reading AND current_reading ≥ new_start, and units = (old_final − previous_reading) + (current_reading − new_start), which keeps units ≥ 0. Both extra values and the reason are stored on the reading row and audited with the entering user's name (D-38); Admin reviews it at approval, the gate that already exists. There is no automatic rollover detection — a rolled dial is entered as a meter replacement. (3) Soft flags, non-blocking, shown as a warn badge on the reading row, on Bill Detail and as a count on Monthly Billing: ใช้สูงผิดปกติ fires only when that room's previous-period usage for the same utility was ≥ 10 units AND current usage exceeds 3× it — below that floor, and for a room with no previous usage at all, no flag is shown; ไม่มีการใช้งาน fires on 0 units for a room with an Active tenant.
decisions.rationale: One hard invariant (units ≥ 0) stops the bug the project exists to prevent, the two replacement fields are cheaper than a meters table and more honest than guessing a digit count, and the usage floor stops the 3× flag firing on every room returning from a vacant month — a badge that cries wolf trains the office to ignore it.

decisions.question: How is the previous reading resolved when a month was missed? (merges Q-E-06)
decisions.decision: previous_reading = the current_reading of the row with the GREATEST period among rows for the same room_id and utility_type whose period is strictly less than the period being saved. Ordering is by period, never by recorded_at, so a month entered late resolves the same way it would have on time; ties are impossible under UNIQUE(room_id, period, utility_type); and the row being written is excluded by construction, so an UPSERT can never take itself as its own previous. If no such row exists, the room's baseline for that utility applies with previous_period = 'baseline' (D-06). Readings taken while the room was vacant count. Periods are not required to be contiguous and a gap never blocks a billing run. When the resolved previous_period is not the immediately preceding month, the reading row and the bill item record it, Bill Detail shows "ครอบคลุมการใช้ตั้งแต่รอบ {previous_period_th}", and the bill's LINE message gets one extra line saying the same (D-31). Units are never split or back-dated across the skipped months, and no bill is created for a skipped period. Reports plot a missing month as a gap in the line, not as zero.
decisions.rationale: Never blocking a month-end is worth more than a back-dating engine nobody asked for; ordering by period rather than by entry time is what makes a late catch-up entry produce the same arithmetic as a punctual one; and one line of Thai copy is what turns a doubled amount from a billing dispute into an explained charge.

decisions.question: How does the phone reading round work — which rooms, saved how, with what progress indicator? (merges Q-U-02)
decisions.decision: The Meter Reading page lists rooms for the selected period, grouped by floor (rooms.floor, D-47) with a sticky floor header, ordered by room code. Four filter chips: ทั้งหมด / ยังไม่จด / จดแล้ว / ห้องว่าง, defaulting to ยังไม่จด. The first three cover billable rooms only (D-07) and drive the counter; ห้องว่าง lists vacant rooms with the badge ไม่ออกบิล so a voluntary reading can be recorded (D-07) without entering the counter. A room counts as จดแล้ว only when BOTH water and electricity are saved for that period. Each room is one card holding Previous (read-only) and Current (numeric input, inputmode="numeric") for water and for electricity, and its own บันทึก button that saves that room alone via one request; the card then collapses to a จดแล้ว summary row. A sticky bottom bar shows "จดแล้ว 42/67 ห้อง" recomputed from the server response after each save. Losing connectivity mid-round loses at most the room being typed: the failed save shows an inline retry that preserves the typed values (D-40). The round is complete when the counter reads Y/Y — the state the acceptance target in D-45 measures.
decisions.rationale: Per-room save is the only design that survives a stairwell with no signal, and the X/Y counter converts "the round is done" from a feeling into a measurable acceptance criterion — which only works if จดแล้ว has one definition and vacant rooms cannot pollute the denominator.

decisions.question: What numeric types hold readings and money, and where is rounding applied? (merges Q-P-02, Q-E-04)
decisions.decision: Readings and units: INT UNSIGNED, whole units only; the input rejects decimals and negatives. Rates: DECIMAL(8,2) — 18.00, 8.00, 35.00 today, and 7.50 is legal. Room area: DECIMAL(6,2). All money: DECIMAL(10,2). FLOAT and DOUBLE are forbidden anywhere in the schema. Rounding: each bill item amount = ROUND(quantity × unit_price, 2) half-up, stored rounded; the bill total = the sum of the already-rounded items, so the printed receipt always equals the sum of its printed lines. There is no second rounding at the total, no rounding to whole baht, and no satang suppression — which is why the receipt's Thai amount in words must handle satang (D-27). JavaScript never does money arithmetic on a total it can recompute — amounts always come from the API as strings formatted by one shared helper (D-03).
decisions.rationale: One rounding rule applied in one place is testable on every surface at once; storing money as DECIMAL removes the 1789.9999999 class of demo-day defect, and constraining rates rather than adding a second rounding rule is how the office avoids satang if it wants to.

decisions.question: Which rate applies when a rate changes, and is it stored on the bill? (merges Q-P-13, Q-E-07, Q-U-19)
decisions.decision: Both: effective-dated rate history AND a snapshot on the bill. The rates table holds (utility_type ENUM('water','electric','common'), unit_price DECIMAL(8,2), effective_from DATE, created_by, created_at) with UNIQUE(utility_type, effective_from) so a same-day tie is impossible; saving a rate in Settings INSERTs a new row with effective_from = today by default (Admin may set a future date) and never UPDATEs an existing row, so history is complete and auditable. Rate resolution is keyed to the PERIOD, not to the moment the button was pressed: generation picks, per utility, the row with the greatest effective_from ≤ the FIRST DAY OF THE BILL'S PERIOD MONTH, and copies unit_price onto the bill item together with the quantity (units, or area for the common fee). Every bill in one period therefore carries the same rate no matter how often or how late generation is re-run (D-18, D-23), so the Dashboard tiles and the monthly report are explainable against a single figure. Every screen, print view and LINE message renders from the bill item's own snapshot; approved bills are never affected by a later rate change. If Draft bills exist for the current period when a rate back-dated into that period is saved, Settings shows "มีบิลฉบับร่าง {N} ใบในรอบนี้ ยังใช้อัตราเดิมอยู่" with a button "คำนวณบิลฉบับร่างใหม่" that recalculates only Draft bills. Defaults seeded with effective_from = the first day of the seed's earliest history period: น้ำ 18.00 บาท/หน่วย, ไฟ 8.00 บาท/หน่วย, ส่วนกลาง 35.00 บาท/ตร.ม. Rates are Admin-only; Staff never see them (D-36).
decisions.rationale: The snapshot is what makes a reprinted receipt and the yearly chart truthful; insert-only history is the same amount of code as an update and gives Settings a defensible audit story. Keying resolution to the period rather than the click is the one line that stops a single month carrying two electricity rates because three rooms were read late.

decisions.question: What triggers bill generation, and what happens when generation runs twice or a reading is corrected afterwards? (merges Q-E-09, Q-U-07, part of Q-P-06)
decisions.decision: Trigger: the Meter Reading page's primary action "ส่งให้นิติตรวจสอบ" (Staff and Admin, enabled once at least one room in the period has both readings) runs generation for that period; Admin can re-run it any time from Monthly Billing via "สร้าง/อัปเดตบิลฉบับร่าง". This one button satisfies PRD §4's ส่งข้อมูลให้นิติตรวจสอบ and §25's flow without adding a submitted state. Idempotency: bills carry UNIQUE(room_id, period). A run creates a Draft bill for every billable room (D-07) that has both readings and no bill; it recalculates in place every existing Draft bill for the period; it never touches a bill that is Unpaid or Paid. Every generated bill always carries exactly three bill_items — water, electric, common — even at 0 units and 0.00 THB (D-41). Saving a corrected reading recalculates that room's Draft bill immediately on save. The run returns and displays a summary: "สร้างบิลใหม่ {a} ใบ · อัปเดต {b} ใบ · ข้าม (อนุมัติแล้ว) {c} ใบ · ยังไม่ได้จด {d} ห้อง".
decisions.rationale: A unique key plus in-place recalculation makes pressing Generate twice — a near-certainty during a demo — a no-op instead of a double-billed room, without a versioning scheme or a delete-and-recreate path that could destroy an approved bill.

decisions.question: How many approval gates are there, can Admin approve many bills at once, and how does a 67-room send avoid a three-minute request? (merges Q-U-06, Q-U-07)
decisions.decision: Exactly one gate. There is no separate reading-approval step: reviewing the readings and approving the bill are the same act, performed on Bill Detail (single bill) or on Monthly Billing (bulk). Only Admin may approve. Monthly Billing gains a row checkbox column, a select-all-in-view checkbox, and a primary button "อนุมัติและส่งบิล ({N} ห้อง)" enabled only when at least one selected bill is Draft; the confirm dialog (D-39) states "อนุมัติและส่งบิล {N} ห้อง ผ่าน LINE — ยกเลิกไม่ได้". Approval and delivery are TWO round trips. (1) The approve call commits every selected bill to Unpaid in one transaction, freezes each bill (D-22), writes one notifications row per bill with status='queued' (D-30) and returns in under five seconds with the result screen. (2) That screen then calls a send endpoint repeatedly, each call pushing at most 20 queued messages and returning running counts, so no single request exceeds roughly twenty seconds and a dropped connection loses nothing — the queued rows survive and the daily job would finish them anyway (D-32). The result summary stays on screen: "อนุมัติ {N} ใบ · ส่ง LINE สำเร็จ {x} · ยังไม่ได้ส่ง (ไม่มี LINE) {y} · ส่งไม่สำเร็จ {z}", with the failed and unsent rooms listed and linked. Bill Detail keeps its single "อนุมัติและส่งบิล" button for the scripted demo of room 205.
decisions.rationale: The four statuses the PRD fixes support exactly one gate — a second gate would need a status the convention forbids. Bulk approval is not a luxury at 67 rooms, but a three-minute synchronous request on free-tier hosting fails in the worst possible way: money committed, browser showing an error, operator re-pressing the button. Queue-then-drain keeps the commit fast and makes the send resumable.

decisions.question: How is the due date derived, and what protects a late approval from producing an unpayable window? (merges Q-P-07)
decisions.decision: Settings holds วันครบกำหนด as a day of month, default 5, Admin-editable, range 1–28. At generation a Draft bill's due_date = that day of its own period month; the Draft screen labels it "กำหนดชำระ 5 ก.ย. 2026 (ยืนยันเมื่ออนุมัติ)". At Approve & Send the due date is recomputed once and frozen as due_date = MAX(day-of-month of the period month, approval_date + 3 days). The PRD §28 example satisfies this exactly: period 2026-09, approval 1 Sep 2026, MAX(5 Sep, 4 Sep) = 5 Sep 2026 — in a live demo the same expression produces approval_date + 3, which is the correct behaviour, not a defect (D-44). The day is clamped to the last day of the month if the month is shorter (the 1–28 range means this cannot bite, but the clamp is written anyway). The due date is never editable by hand — there is no per-bill due date field — and every bill in one approval batch approved on the same day gets the same due date.
decisions.rationale: Tenants expect the same date every month, and the single MAX() expression guarantees at least three days to pay without a month-rolling rule, which is what keeps the D−2 reminder in D-33 from ever being scheduled in the past.

decisions.question: Exactly when does a bill become Overdue, who makes it happen, and does it add a charge? (merges Q-P-08, Q-E-11, Q-U-11)
decisions.decision: Overdue is DERIVED, never stored, and there is no late fee, interest or penalty of any kind. bills.status stores only 'Draft', 'Unpaid', 'Paid'. One shared helper — a single SQL expression CASE WHEN status='Unpaid' AND due_date < CURDATE() THEN 'Overdue' ELSE status END, and one JS function billStatus(bill) — produces the four-value display status. The rule is a DISPLAY rule: any surface that shows a status to a human, or filters or counts by a status a human can see, must go through the helper. Aggregation that deliberately means "approved" or "not yet settled" — D-41's money tiles reading status IN ('Unpaid','Paid'), D-42's arrears report ageing every Unpaid bill — reads the stored column directly and is not a defect. The transition is instantaneous at 00:00 Asia/Bangkok on the day after the due date, with no job, no drift and nothing to fail. Paying an overdue bill sets status='Paid' and the display status follows. The daily job (D-32) sends overdue reminders but changes no status.
decisions.rationale: A stored status that depends on a cron job on free-tier hosting reads as a broken feature the moment the instance sleeps; a derived status is always correct, survives a demo on a laptop, and makes the expected value in every test deterministic. Stating the rule as a display rule rather than an absolute ban keeps it from being ignored where it matters.

decisions.question: What is frozen at approval, and what is the sanctioned way to correct a bill already sent or already paid? (merges Q-P-04, Q-P-05 correction half, Q-E-10)
decisions.decision: At Approve & Send the bill is frozen: readings, units, unit prices, room area, tenant name, line amounts, total and due date are all snapshots and none may be edited afterwards through any endpoint. Correcting an Unpaid or Overdue bill: Admin presses "ตีกลับเป็นฉบับร่าง" on Bill Detail, supplies a Thai reason (min 10 characters), the system writes an audit row with before/after JSON and sets the bill back to Draft, unfreezing its readings (D-12). The button is available ONLY on a room's most recent bill; where a later bill exists for the same room it is disabled with "มีบิลรอบถัดไปแล้ว ไม่สามารถแก้ไขย้อนหลังได้ — กรุณาแก้ในรอบล่าสุด", because a later bill's previous_reading is a snapshot of the value being edited (D-12). After editing and re-approving, the LINE bill is re-sent as BILL_CORRECTED (D-31). Correcting a PAID bill is a counter transaction, not a system transaction: the cash goes back across the counter first, then Admin voids the payment (D-25) — whose dialog reads "คืนเงินสด {amount} บาท ให้ผู้เช่าก่อนยืนยันการยกเลิก" — the old receipt is stamped ยกเลิก, the bill returns to Unpaid, is reverted to Draft, corrected, re-approved, and paid fresh at the full corrected amount with a new receipt number; the corrected LINE message carries the extra line "ยอดที่ชำระไว้เดิมได้คืนเป็นเงินสดแล้ว กรุณาชำระตามยอดใหม่". The system never holds a credit, a refund or a balance. There is no Cancelled or Void bill status, no adjustment line item, and no credit carried to the next month.
decisions.rationale: One reversible path covers both cases, keeps exactly four statuses, and makes the write guard a single check on bill.status in the middleware. Restricting the revert to the newest bill is the one rule that keeps the previous-reading chain honest, and routing the refund across the counter is what lets the system stay free of money it does not hold.

decisions.question: What happens to an occupied room whose readings are missing when the run executes? (merges part of Q-P-14, Q-U-09)
decisions.decision: The room is simply excluded from that run — no bill, no zero-unit bill, no placeholder. Monthly Billing shows a persistent warn callout at the top of the period whenever any billable room lacks a bill: "ยังไม่ได้จดมิเตอร์ {N} ห้อง: 108, 312, 405 — ยังไม่ได้สร้างบิล", the room codes linking straight to the Meter Reading page for that room. Approval is NOT blocked: the office may approve the bills that exist. When the missing rooms are read later, re-running generation (D-18) creates only their bills, at the same rate as the rest of the period (D-17); they are approved in a second, smaller batch and get their own due date under D-20. The count of billable rooms without a bill is the single figure that drives both this banner and the completeness line in D-11, and it is the tester's assertion for "ทุกห้องที่มีผู้เช่าได้รับบิล": it must reach 0. Nothing is "closed" — there is no such state (D-11).
decisions.rationale: A hard block would stop the office billing 66 rooms because one meter is behind a locked door. The banner makes the gap impossible to miss, the idempotent re-run makes filling it a one-click operation, and one shared count means the banner and the acceptance criterion can never disagree.

decisions.question: Does the counter record the exact bill total, is a partial payment allowed, and is change shown? (merges Q-P-03, Q-U-12)
decisions.decision: Full payment only, one live payment per bill. The stored payment amount is fixed at the bill total and is not an input — the Payment screen shows ยอดที่ต้องชำระ 1,790.00 บาท as read-only text, with the room and the billing period in the header. Above the confirm button there is an optional cashier aid: a numeric field รับเงิน that computes เงินทอน on screen live (รับเงิน 2,000 → เงินทอน 210.00); neither value is stored, printed on the receipt, or sent to the API. Confirm Cash Payment (Admin only, D-36) writes one payments row (bill_id, amount, paid_at, received_by_user_id, method='cash'), flips the bill to Paid, issues the receipt (D-27) and queues the LINE confirmation (D-31) — one transaction, one button, no second screen. Partial payment is a documented v1 limitation (D-05): a tenant who is short is asked to return with the full amount; the bill stays รอชำระ / เกินกำหนด.
decisions.rationale: PRD §12 models exactly one button and one status flip; keeping the amount non-editable means Paid always means fully paid, no fifth status is needed, no SUM appears in any query, and overpayment cannot exist — which is what lets D-25 be a simple void with no refund or credit machinery inside the system.

decisions.question: How is a payment recorded against the wrong room or the wrong month undone? (merges Q-P-05, Q-U-13)
decisions.decision: Admin only, from Bill Detail or the Receipt view: "ยกเลิกการชำระเงิน" with a required Thai reason (min 10 characters). The cash is returned across the counter FIRST — the dialog says so explicitly (D-39). The effect: the payment row is marked voided (voided_at, voided_by, void_reason) and never deleted; the receipt row is marked voided and never deleted, so it KEEPS ITS NUMBER — that, and not gaplessness, is what voiding rather than deleting buys (D-27) — and every view or print of it is stamped ยกเลิก in red across the header; the bill returns to Unpaid and therefore displays as Overdue automatically if the due date has passed (D-21); an audit row is written. No LINE message is sent on the void itself — the office explains in person. A bill whose most recent payment was voided is EXCLUDED from automatic PRE_DUE and OVERDUE sends (D-33) and shows the badge ระงับการแจ้งเตือนอัตโนมัติ, so the system never sends ⚠️ เลยกำหนดชำระแล้ว to a tenant who paid and did nothing wrong; Admin may still use the per-bill manual resend once the situation has been explained. Because the payment amount always equals the bill total (D-24) there is no overpayment, no refund inside the system and no credit note anywhere.
decisions.rationale: Mis-keying a room number at a cash counter is a weekly event and was otherwise only fixable by editing the database. Voiding rather than deleting keeps the audit trail and the receipt number intact, and suppressing the automated chase is one WHERE clause that stops the system contradicting its own policy of silence.

decisions.question: How are a double-clicked confirm, two cashiers on one bill, and concurrent receipt numbering prevented from producing duplicates? (merges Q-E-19)
decisions.decision: Correctness lives in the database, not the browser. MySQL 8 has no partial indexes, so the one-live-payment-per-bill rule is enforced with a stored generated column: payments.active_bill_id BIGINT UNSIGNED AS (IF(voided_at IS NULL, bill_id, NULL)) STORED, with UNIQUE(active_bill_id). MySQL permits repeated NULLs in a unique index, so any number of voided payments coexist with at most one live payment per bill and D-25's void-then-repay path works unchanged. This mechanism is binding: it must not be "simplified" into a filtered index (which does not exist) or a plain UNIQUE(bill_id) (which would make a corrected bill unpayable forever). Also: UNIQUE(payment_id) on receipts; the status change is a conditional update — UPDATE bills SET status='Paid' WHERE id=? AND status='Unpaid' — failing with the Thai message "บิลนี้ถูกชำระไปแล้ว" if 0 rows are affected; receipt numbers come from a single counters row allocated inside the same transaction with INSERT INTO counters (name, seq) VALUES ('receipt',1) ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE seq = LAST_INSERT_ID(seq+1), read back with LAST_INSERT_ID(). The UI additionally disables the button and shows a spinner on submit — a courtesy, never the guarantee. A rolled-back transaction may consume a number and leave a gap; gaps are accepted and documented (D-27), duplicates are not.
decisions.rationale: Two receipts for one payment, or a Dashboard reporting 3,580 collected on a 1,790 bill, is the kind of defect that cannot be argued away in a demo. A generated column, a conditional update and an atomic counter make it impossible using only constructs the chosen database actually has.

decisions.question: Is the receipt a tax invoice, what must it carry, and how are numbers allocated? (merges Q-P-18, Q-U-16)
decisions.decision: A non-tax ใบเสร็จรับเงิน. No VAT, no VAT breakdown, no ใบกำกับภาษี, no toggle. Required fields in order: apartment name / address / โทร from Settings, plus เลขประจำตัวผู้เสียภาษี which is OPTIONAL and renders only when Settings holds one (letterhead, D-01); the title ใบเสร็จรับเงิน; เลขที่ REC-202609-000852; วันที่ชำระ 3 กันยายน 2026; ห้อง 205; ชื่อผู้เช่า (snapshot); รอบบิล กันยายน 2026; the three line items, always all three (D-41), each with quantity, unit price and amount (ค่าน้ำ 10 หน่วย × 18.00 = 180.00 / ค่าไฟ 70 หน่วย × 8.00 = 560.00 / ค่าส่วนกลาง 30 ตร.ม. × 35.00 = 1,050.00); ยอดรวม 1,790.00 บาท plus the Thai amount in words; ชำระโดย เงินสด; ผู้รับเงิน (the Admin's ชื่อที่แสดง, D-46); a signature line ลงชื่อผู้รับเงิน. Amount in words has two forms and one shared helper: an integer total renders "{words}บาทถ้วน" (หนึ่งพันเจ็ดร้อยเก้าสิบบาทถ้วน), a total carrying satang renders "{words}บาท{satang words}สตางค์" — satang is reachable because rates may be 7.50 (D-16). The helper is a named deliverable with one unit test covering 0, 1,790.00, 1,790.50 and 1,000,000.00. Numbering: REC-<payment month YYYYMM>-<6-digit zero-padded sequence>, one continuous counter that NEVER resets, allocated inside the payment transaction (D-26). The sequence is UNIQUE and MONOTONIC but NOT GAPLESS — gaps arise legitimately from rolled-back transactions and from the seed's starting offset (D-44), and no document, rationale or test may claim otherwise; the tester's two assertions are that no two receipts share a number and that a later payment never receives a lower one. Copies are button-driven, not browser-driven: the receipt route renders the original while print_count = 0, and the primary button พิมพ์ใบเสร็จ POSTs to increment print_count before calling window.print(); every render at print_count ≥ 1 carries the สำเนา mark and the button reads พิมพ์สำเนา. Printing from the browser's own menu bypasses the counter and yields an unmarked copy — an accepted limitation (D-05). A voided receipt prints stamped ยกเลิก (D-25).
decisions.rationale: Matches the PRD's own example number, which a monthly reset could not produce in a 67-room building, and avoids issuing tax documents a student project cannot substantiate. A button-driven copy mark is the only version a tester can pass or fail, and stating plainly that the sequence is not gapless stops a QA case that would fail on the seed before the app is even opened.

decisions.question: What paper size and print mechanism, and what does the paper bill look like? (merges Q-U-15)
decisions.decision: A5 portrait through the browser's own print dialog: window.print() on a dedicated route with @page { size: A5 portrait; margin: 10mm } and a print stylesheet that hides the app chrome. No PDF library, no server-side rendering, no thermal-printer layout, no printer driver assumptions. The receipt must fit on exactly one A5 page with the three line items, the total and the number — a QA check. The same route serves the on-screen view (framed with .device.print in the documentation) and the printed page. The paper bill uses the same machinery: ใบแจ้งค่าใช้จ่าย is the D-27 layout on the same A5 route, titled ใบแจ้งค่าใช้จ่าย, carrying the letterhead, ห้อง, ชื่อผู้เช่า, รอบบิล, กำหนดชำระ {due_date} and the same three line items with units, rate and amount — and NO receipt number, no payment date, no ผู้รับเงิน and no signature line. It is available on Bill Detail (button พิมพ์ใบแจ้งหนี้) for any bill that is not Draft, and is the hand-over path for tenants with no LINE binding (D-30).
decisions.rationale: Zero dependencies and zero hardware assumptions; A5 comfortably holds the content, and a print stylesheet is a few rules against a PDF pipeline that would need its own Thai font embedding. Specifying the invoice here rather than leaving it as a clause matters because on day one it is the common case, not the fallback.

decisions.question: How does a tenant's LINE User ID actually reach the Tenants record? (merges Q-E-13)
decisions.decision: Messaging API webhook plus a one-time code — no LIFF, no app, no manual pasting of user IDs. Flow: (1) Admin presses "สร้างรหัสผูก LINE" on the tenant's row; the system generates a 6-character code from the alphabet ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZ23456789 (no O/0/I/1), valid 7 days, single use, displayed and printable on a slip with the OA QR code. (2) The tenant adds the Official Account as a friend; the follow event stores the userId in a pending table with the display name. (3) The tenant sends the code as a chat message; the webhook matches it, binds userId to the tenant, expires the code, and replies "✅ ผูกบัญชีสำเร็จ\nคุณจะได้รับบิลและประกาศของห้อง {room_code} ผ่าน LINE นี้". A wrong or expired code gets "❌ ไม่พบรหัสนี้ หรือรหัสหมดอายุแล้ว กรุณาติดต่อสำนักงานนิติบุคคล". Any other inbound message gets one fixed auto-reply pointing at the office; the OA is not a chatbot. Uniqueness is on the TENANT, not on the LINE account: UNIQUE(tenant_id) on the binding, so one LINE account may be bound to several Active tenants — a parent renting two rooms, or a couple sharing a phone — and every template names the room, so nothing is ambiguous; a message to a userId bound to two tenants is two notifications rows, one per bill. A code sent from an already-bound account gets the normal success reply naming the new room. The Tenants page shows the binding (LINE display name + linked date) and a "ยกเลิกการผูก" action for Admin; ending a tenancy unbinds only that tenancy (D-08). Webhook route: POST /line/webhook, exempt from session auth and CSRF, verified by X-Line-Signature, and it returns 200 BEFORE doing any work so a cold start still ACKs inside LINE's timeout (D-43).
decisions.rationale: A tenant cannot read their own userId anywhere in LINE, so staff literally cannot type it — this flow is the only self-service option that uses nothing but the Messaging API, and the printed code makes the room binding verified rather than guessed. Keying uniqueness to the tenant is what stops the second room in a family silently stealing the first room's binding.

decisions.question: What happens at Approve & Send when the tenant has no linked LINE account or the send fails? (merges Q-P-19, Q-E-14, Q-E-16, Q-U-10)
decisions.decision: Money state and messaging state are independent. The status change is committed FIRST and the send happens after, outside the transaction — a LINE outage can never prevent billing and never rolls anything back (D-19). One notifications table covers bills AND announcements: (id, type, bill_id NULL, announcement_id NULL, tenant_id, recipient_user_id, status ENUM('queued','sent','failed','skipped_no_line'), attempt_count INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, last_error, http_status, last_attempt_at, send_date) with UNIQUE(type, bill_id, announcement_id, tenant_id, send_date). One row per RECIPIENT, never one per API call, so a 54-recipient multicast writes 54 rows and D-35's per-announcement result and D-34's monthly count are the same query. Retries UPDATE the row rather than needing a new one: every attempt — first send, daily retry, manual ส่งซ้ำ — is an UPSERT that increments attempt_count and rewrites status; automatic retries stop at attempt_count = 3, the Admin's manual button is never capped. A corrected bill re-sent the same day writes type='BILL_CORRECTED', its own key. Per-bill delivery state, badged on Monthly Billing and Bill Detail: ส่งแล้ว (ok), ยังไม่ได้ส่ง — ไม่มี LINE (neutral, skipped_no_line), ส่งไม่สำเร็จ (bad, error on hover). Unbinding happens ONLY on an explicit 400 invalid-userId from the push endpoint, and never for the seed's placeholder IDs (D-44); a tenant who has BLOCKED the Official Account is not reported to us at all — LINE returns 200 and drops the message — so the word "blocked" appears in no badge, report or test case, and the gap is a listed limitation (D-05). Bills never delivered are handed over on paper: Bill Detail's พิมพ์ใบแจ้งหนี้ (D-28). Approval is never blocked by delivery.
decisions.rationale: On day one almost no tenant is linked, so the unlinked case is the common case. Recording delivery per recipient is what makes ส่งบิลผ่าน LINE OA verifiable, gives the demo an honest failure path, and lets one table serve bills and announcements; an UPSERT with a counter is what makes the retry policy the decision already promised actually expressible.

decisions.question: What is the exact Thai text of every outbound message?
decisions.rationale: These strings are the only part of the system a tenant ever reads, and they appear in the PRD, the UI mockups, the test plan and the demo script — one source of truth prevents four different versions. Braces everywhere prevent the second-worst outcome: a designer mocking up ห้อง 205 for every room and a tester asserting on a literal that only one room can satisfy.

decisions.question: What actually runs the scheduled reminders on free-tier hosting, and how is duplicate sending prevented? (merges Q-E-12, part of Q-U-11)
decisions.decision: One authenticated endpoint plus one external cron. POST /internal/jobs/daily, guarded by a shared secret in the X-Job-Token header (env var), called every day at 09:00 Asia/Bangkok by a free external scheduler (cron-job.org, or a Render Cron Job). No node-cron inside the process. Keeping the instance awake is a SEPARATE schedule and not this job's business: a 10-minute GET /healthz ping (D-43). Idempotency has two layers: a job_runs table with UNIQUE(job_name, run_date) so a repeated ping the same day is a no-op, and the notifications key from D-30 so no bill receives the same message type twice in one day. The job_runs guard applies ONLY to the scheduled path: Settings carries an Admin button "รันงานแจ้งเตือนตอนนี้" that calls the identical code with job_name='daily_manual' and does not consult job_runs at all, so a demo held at 14:00 can still trigger reminders after the 09:00 cron has already run — safety comes from the notifications key, which is enough. The button reports what it sent: "ส่งแจ้งเตือนก่อนครบกำหนด {a} ราย · เลยกำหนด {b} ราย · ส่งซ้ำที่ล้มเหลว {c} ราย". The job also drains any notifications rows left queued by a bulk approval (D-19). It never changes a bill status (D-21).
decisions.rationale: An in-process scheduler silently never fires on a sleeping free service, which would make the headline automatic-notification feature undemonstrable. One endpoint plus two unique keys gives real automation and protection against a retrying scheduler — but the demo button must not inherit the daily guard, or the feature is undemonstrable for a second reason.

decisions.question: On which days and at what hour do reminders fire, how often do they repeat, and is there a manual send? (merges Q-P-09)
decisions.decision: The daily job at 09:00 Asia/Bangkok sends, per bill, at most four automatic messages in its entire life: PRE_DUE on due_date − 2 days; OVERDUE on due_date + 1 day, + 8 days and + 15 days (the condition is literally days_overdue IN (1, 8, 15)). Nothing is sent after day 15, nothing is sent to a Paid bill, nothing is sent outside 09:00 — no evening or weekend send — and nothing is sent for a bill whose most recent payment was voided (D-25), which is one extra WHERE clause and one tester assertion. In addition Admin has a per-bill manual "ส่งแจ้งเตือนอีกครั้ง" button on Bill Detail; it is not capped, because it is the tool of last resort on exactly the day an automatic send failed (D-30). Announcements are unaffected by this schedule and are sent on demand (D-35).
decisions.rationale: Two automatic touches plus two capped weekly nudges is what an office needs for arrears follow-up; a ceiling of four messages and a single fixed hour keeps tenants from blocking the Official Account, which would also destroy bill delivery invisibly (D-30). The IN (1,8,15) condition is one line and one obvious test.

decisions.question: Which LINE API is used for which message, and how does the design stay inside the message quota? (merges Q-E-15)
decisions.decision: Push API for everything personalised (bill, corrected bill, pre-due, overdue, payment confirmation, link replies) — one call per recipient, because the content differs per room. Multicast API in chunks of at most 500 userIds for announcements, which share identical text; one notifications row per recipient regardless (D-30). Broadcast is never used, because it would reach every OA follower including ex-tenants. Quota visibility rather than quota machinery: the LINE OA free plan allows 500 push/multicast messages per month, and Settings shows one line, "ส่งข้อความเดือนนี้: {N}/500", where N = COUNT(*) over notifications WHERE status='sent' for the current month — failed and skipped_no_line rows never inflate it — rendered in warn colour above 450. Nothing is throttled or blocked; exhausting the allowance silently stops delivery and is a listed limitation (D-05). โหมดทดสอบ LINE in Settings redirects every outbound message to a single whitelisted userId with the intended recipient still recorded on the notifications row, and it DEFAULTS TO ON in every environment — it is switched off only for the rehearsed demo path, which sends to the two or three real accounts the team owns.
decisions.rationale: Multicast cuts announcement API calls from 67 to 1. Naming the 500 ceiling turns a vague worry into a number the office can watch, counting only successful sends keeps it honest, and defaulting test mode ON is what stops a single rehearsal spending the month's allowance and wiping the seeded bindings (D-44).

decisions.question: Who receives an announcement, is it previewed, and can it be recalled? (merges Q-U-17)
decisions.decision: Audience selector with two options only: ทุกห้องที่มีผู้เช่า (default) or เลือกชั้น (a multi-select over rooms.floor, D-47). No per-room selection, no unpaid-only audience, no scheduling. The form is หัวข้อ (max 60 chars) + เนื้อหา (max 400 chars, keeping the whole message far under LINE's 5,000-character limit), with a live preview rendered exactly as the ANNOUNCEMENT template in D-31 and a live recipient count "จะส่งถึง {rooms} ห้อง (ผู้เช่าที่ผูก LINE แล้ว {linked} ราย)" — the second number matters, because unlinked tenants receive nothing. Admin only. The confirm dialog states the count and that it cannot be undone (D-39). Delivery is recorded one notifications row per recipient tenant against announcement_id (D-30), so the Announcements list shows each announcement's sent time, audience, recipient count and delivery result, and the monthly message count (D-34) includes announcements. A sent announcement is immutable history: viewable, never editable, resendable or recallable. LINE offers no recall and the UI must not imply otherwise.
decisions.rationale: The one real-world case beyond a building-wide notice is a floor-scoped water shut-off, and floor filtering is a WHERE clause over a column the Rooms table already holds. Showing the linked count next to the room count stops the office believing 67 people were told when only 54 were, and per-recipient rows are what make that number a fact rather than an estimate.

decisions.question: How many roles exist and exactly what may each one do — in particular, may Staff take cash? (merges Q-P-15, Q-E-18)
decisions.decision: Two roles, admin and staff, on a single users.role column. The PRD §12 sentence "เจ้าหน้าที่กด Confirm Cash Payment" is a drafting error and is corrected: the counter is operated by an Admin login, matching §4, which grants รับชำระเงิน and ออกใบเสร็จ to Admin only. Permission matrix, binding for the middleware, the navigation and the test plan — admin: every page and every action, including rates, bill generation, approval, revert to Draft, payment, void payment, receipts, announcements, tenants, users, reports, settings and the manual job trigger. staff: ภาพรวม (a reduced Dashboard showing only room counts and this period's reading progress), ห้องพัก (read-only list and detail, no rates and no amounts), จดมิเตอร์ (create and edit readings per D-12, record a meter replacement per D-13, and press ส่งให้นิติตรวจสอบ per D-18), and the reading history of a room. Staff never see a bill amount, a rate, a payment, a receipt, the Tenants page, the Users page or Settings — money is not merely hidden in the navigation, it is absent from the API responses staff receive. There is no third role and no per-user permission table.
decisions.rationale: Two roles is the smallest matrix that still separates the person who reads a meter from the person who approves the money built from it, and it is exactly the role list PRD §4 defines. One middleware plus one documented table replaces a third of the guesswork in the test plan.

decisions.question: Session or JWT, and where does session state live on a free instance that restarts? (merges Q-E-17)
decisions.decision: express-session with a MySQL-backed session store (express-mysql-session), cookie httpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Secure in production, rolling 8-hour expiry. No JWT, no refresh tokens, no localStorage tokens. Passwords hashed with bcrypt, cost 10; no self-service password reset in v1 — Admin resets another user's password from the Users page (D-46). The seeded admin password is NOT committed: seed.sql reads it from the environment variable SEED_ADMIN_PASSWORD and seeding fails if it is unset; the runbook documents the variable, never a value, and first login forces a change. Logout deletes the session row. The LINE webhook route is exempt from session auth and CSRF and is authenticated by X-Line-Signature; the internal job endpoint is exempt and authenticated by X-Job-Token (D-32); /healthz is public. Every other POST is protected by a CSRF token. Rate limiting: 10 failed logins per IP per 15 minutes, with app.set('trust proxy', 1) so the limiter keys on the real client IP behind Render's TLS-terminating proxy rather than bucketing every visitor together; the limiter never applies to the webhook, the job endpoint or /healthz.
decisions.rationale: Revocation and logout come free, the MySQL instance is already provisioned, and a DB-backed store survives the free-tier restarts that would log everyone out mid-demo. The two operational lines matter more than they look: without trust proxy one wrong password locks the whole demo out, and a committed admin password on a public HTTPS URL is a working credential in a public repo.

decisions.question: Which actions are audited, and in what structure? (merges Q-E-20)
decisions.decision: One audit_log table: (id, entity_type, entity_id, bill_id NULL, action, actor_user_id, before_json, after_json, reason, created_at), written through a single helper called inside the same transaction as the change. Audited actions, exactly these twelve: bill approve, bill revert to Draft (with reason), payment confirm, payment void (with reason), rate change, room create/edit, room AREA change (called out separately because it silently changes every future common-area fee, D-09), room deactivate, meter reading create, meter reading edit, meter replacement (with reason), tenant LINE link/unlink, announcement send. Not audited: logins, page views, report exports, Settings profile edits. bill_id is set on every row attributable to a bill — approve, revert, payment confirm, payment void, and reading edits made while that bill was Draft — so Bill Detail's Admin-only timeline is exactly SELECT * FROM audit_log WHERE bill_id = ? ORDER BY created_at, with no cross-entity join to invent and one obvious test. The columns the PRD names explicitly stay where they are: payments.received_by_user_id, meter_readings.recorded_by, rates.created_by. There is no global audit browser screen in v1.
decisions.rationale: One generic table plus one insert helper answers "who changed the electricity rate before this bill was approved" — precisely the business-logic question a demo reviewer asks — for far less than per-table tracking columns. The bill_id column is what turns the timeline from an invented query into a one-line one, and auditing area changes closes the only unlogged path to future money.

decisions.question: Which actions need a confirmation dialog and what must it say? (merges Q-U-14)
decisions.decision: One shared dialog component, six call sites, never the browser's native confirm(). Every dialog states the exact effect with counts and names the irreversibility in Thai; the primary button repeats the verb rather than saying ตกลง. The six: (1) Approve & Send single — "อนุมัติและส่งบิลห้อง {room_code} ผ่าน LINE — ยกเลิกไม่ได้" / button อนุมัติและส่ง; (2) bulk approve — "อนุมัติและส่งบิล {N} ห้อง ผ่าน LINE — ยกเลิกไม่ได้"; (3) Confirm Cash Payment — "ยืนยันรับเงินสด {total} บาท · ห้อง {room_code} · รอบ {period_th} และออกใบเสร็จ", the billing period included because a room in arrears has several unpaid bills and paying the wrong month is precisely the mistake D-25 exists to undo; (4) send announcement — "ส่งประกาศถึง {N} ห้อง ผ่าน LINE — เรียกคืนไม่ได้"; (5) void payment — "คืนเงินสด {total} บาท ให้ผู้เช่าก่อนยืนยันการยกเลิก", reason field required before the primary button enables; (6) end a tenancy / deactivate a room — reason field required, and the dialog states what will be kept ("ประวัติบิลและใบเสร็จจะยังคงอยู่"). No typed-name confirmations anywhere. No toast-with-undo pattern anywhere, because an undo window would force outbound LINE messages into a queue.
decisions.rationale: These are exactly the actions that reach real phones or real cash and cannot be taken back. One component gives the designer a single spec, the engineer six call sites and the tester six one-line assertions.

decisions.question: What is the standard treatment for unauthorized access, empty lists and failed saves? (merges Q-U-04)
decisions.decision: Unauthorized: a staff user opening an Admin URL directly gets a Thai 403 page — "ไม่มีสิทธิ์เข้าถึงหน้านี้ · บัญชีของคุณเป็นเจ้าหน้าที่ กรุณาติดต่อนิติบุคคล" with a button back to จดมิเตอร์ — never a silent redirect, so the permission matrix is testable row by row; the API returns 403 with a JSON error code. Empty states: one shared component (a muted icon, one Thai sentence, and where relevant one primary action), specified for all eight list surfaces — ห้องพัก "ยังไม่มีข้อมูลห้อง" + เพิ่มห้อง; ผู้เช่า "ยังไม่มีผู้เช่า"; จดมิเตอร์ "ยังไม่มีห้องที่ต้องจดในรอบนี้"; บิลประจำเดือน "ยังไม่มีบิลในรอบนี้" + สร้างบิลฉบับร่าง; รับชำระเงิน "ค้นหาห้องเพื่อรับชำระเงิน"; ประกาศ "ยังไม่เคยส่งประกาศ"; รายงาน "ยังไม่มีข้อมูลในช่วงเวลานี้"; the arrears list "ไม่มีห้องค้างชำระ 🎉". Failed save: an inline error above the form that preserves every typed value and offers ลองอีกครั้ง — never a redirect, never a lost form, and on the phone reading screen never a full-page reload. Loading: skeleton rows for lists, a spinner with a disabled button for actions.
decisions.rationale: An explicit 403 turns the permission matrix into a checklist a tester can walk; one empty-state component prevents eight blank white areas appearing in front of the examiners; preserving values on a failed save is the difference between a usable and an unusable phone screen in a stairwell.

decisions.question: What is on the Users page, and how does a locked-out account get back in?
decisions.decision: Users = ผู้ใช้งานระบบ (added to the page mapping in D-02), Admin only, satisfying PRD §18 function 3. Fields: ชื่อผู้ใช้ (unique), ชื่อที่แสดง — which is what prints as ผู้รับเงิน on the receipt (D-27) — บทบาท (admin/staff), สถานะ (Active/Inactive), and the action ตั้งรหัสผ่านใหม่, which is the ONLY password recovery path in v1 (D-37). Users are never deleted, only set Inactive, because payments.received_by_user_id, meter_readings.recorded_by and rates.created_by reference them. No email address, no self-service reset, no invitation flow. An Inactive user cannot log in and keeps every historical attribution.
decisions.rationale: Three decisions already depended on a Users page that no decision had created, leaving the designer without a label, the engineer without a field list and the tester without a permission row — and a staff account locked out during the demo with no way back in.

decisions.question: What is the exact formula and time scope of every Dashboard figure? (merges Q-U-18)
decisions.decision: Every KPI is scoped to a selected billing period, defaulting to the current calendar month, chosen by one month picker at the top of the page. Every generated bill always carries exactly three bill_items — water, electric, common — even at 0 units and 0.00 THB (D-18), so the tiles always sum to the total, the receipt always prints three lines, and D-42's split columns are never null; a bill with fewer than three items is a defect with its own assertion. Formulas, binding: ห้องทั้งหมด = COUNT(rooms); มีผู้เช่า = COUNT(rooms WHERE status='Occupied'); ห้องว่าง = the difference. ยอดค่าน้ำเดือนนี้ / ยอดค่าไฟเดือนนี้ / ยอดค่าส่วนกลาง = SUM(bill_items.amount) by type over approved bills of that period. ยอดเรียกเก็บทั้งหมด = SUM(bills.total) over approved bills of that period, where approved means the STORED status is Unpaid or Paid — Draft bills are excluded from every money figure on this page, and reading the stored column for this purpose is explicitly not a violation of D-21. รับชำระแล้ว = SUM(bills.total) WHERE status='Paid' for that period (counted by billing period, not by payment date). ค้างชำระ = ยอดเรียกเก็บทั้งหมด − รับชำระแล้ว, which by construction equals the sum of the Unpaid and Overdue bills of that period, so the three tiles always reconcile on screen. One additional tile, explicitly all-time: ค้างชำระสะสมทุกงวด = SUM(total) over every Unpaid bill of every period. Charts: 12-month water units, 12-month electricity units, 12-month revenue collected, and a Paid vs Unpaid+Overdue count for the selected period. Staff see only the room-count tiles and the reading progress (D-36).
decisions.rationale: Eight numbers with no formulas is eight arguments between developers and zero possible test assertions. Billed minus collected must equal outstanding on screen, and that identity only holds when all three read the same period, exclude Draft, and every bill carries all three items.

decisions.question: What is the minimum report set and is it exportable? (merges Q-P-20)
decisions.decision: Exactly four reports, each on screen and each with a CSV export produced by one shared helper (UTF-8 with BOM so Excel opens Thai correctly, filename pattern report-{name}-{period}.csv). (1) สรุปการเรียกเก็บและรับชำระรายเดือน — per period: billed, collected, outstanding, each split water / electricity / common fee, plus bill counts by status. (2) รายการค้างชำระ — every Unpaid bill across all periods, aged into non-overlapping buckets 1-7 / 8-30 / 31-60 / 61+ วัน, sorted by days overdue descending, showing room, tenant, phone, period, amount, due date, days late; the four bucket counts must sum to the row count and the four bucket amounts to the report total — one assertion each. (3) ประวัติรายห้อง 12 เดือน — one room, 12 periods: water units, electricity units, each amount, total, status, payment date, receipt number — the screen the office opens when a tenant disputes a reading. (4) ห้องที่ใช้น้ำ/ไฟสูงสุด — top 10 by units for the selected period, with each room's own previous-month comparison. No PDF export, no report builder, no ad-hoc column chooser. Admin only.
decisions.rationale: These four cover exactly the month-end job the PRD describes — what was billed, what was collected, who owes and for how long, and one room's history — and report 3 is what makes PRD §3 objective 10 demonstrable. CSV is one endpoint that stops the office re-typing figures into Excel.

decisions.question: Where does the app run, how does the webhook get a stable HTTPS URL, and what is the backup plan? (merges Q-E-21)
decisions.decision: Render free web service running a single long-lived Node.js + Express process (server-rendered EJS pages plus Chart.js, no separate frontend build) — one fixed HTTPS URL for the LINE webhook for the life of the project, which is the requirement Vercel's serverless model cannot meet. Database: a free managed MySQL 8 (Aiven or Clever Cloud), connection string in environment variables. Staying awake is its own schedule: a free external scheduler pings GET /healthz every 10 MINUTES — the 09:00 daily job (D-32) is not a keep-alive, because a Render free service spins down after roughly 15 minutes of inactivity and a once-a-day request keeps it up for one minute. Belt and braces: /line/webhook returns 200 before doing any work, so even a cold start ACKs inside LINE's timeout and the endpoint is never auto-disabled for repeated delivery failures — which would silently kill the linking flow in D-29, the only way a userId ever reaches the system. The runbook adds one line: re-verify the webhook URL in the LINE console after every deploy and before the demo. Recovery: seed.sql is committed and recreates the entire demo dataset from an empty database in one command (D-44); a mysqldump is taken and committed before every milestone and on the day before the final demo; the LINE channel secret and access token live only in environment variables and a password-protected team note, never in the repo. Documented fallback for demo day if the hosted DB is unreachable: run the same app locally against a local MySQL restored from seed.sql, webhook disabled, LINE test mode on (D-34).
decisions.rationale: A stable webhook URL and a real long-lived process are hard requirements the LINE integration cannot work without, and both are free on Render. Separating the uptime ping from the reminder job is the difference between a webhook that answers and one that cold-starts into a timeout; a committed seed.sql means the graded demo can be rebuilt in minutes if the free database vanishes.

decisions.question: What seed data must exist for the demo, and how do the PRD §16 and §28 figures relate to it?
decisions.decision: seed.sql computes every date RELATIVE TO THE RUN DATE, because three other decisions make fixed dates wrong on any real demo day: D-20 freezes due_date = MAX(due day, approval + 3 days), D-21 derives Overdue from CURDATE(), D-27 builds the receipt number from the payment month. The current period is DATE_FORMAT(CURDATE(),'%Y-%m'); the twelve history periods are the eleven preceding months plus the current one; room 205's reading round is dated the 1st of the current month; its bill is left DRAFT so the demo approves it live; the receipt counter is seeded so room 205's payment issues REC-<current YYYYMM>-000852. BINDING ON EVERY DOCUMENT: the fixed dates of PRD §28 — 5 ก.ย. 2026, 3 ก.ย. 2026, REC-202609-000852 — are documentation and mockup values; the live demo reproduces the ARITHMETIC (10 หน่วย, 70 หน่วย, 180, 560, 1,050, 1,790 บาท, room 205 at 30 ตร.ม.), never the calendar. Contents: 80 rooms across 5 floors, 101-116 … 501-516, ALL of them 30.00 ตร.ม. (a uniform studio block, so nothing looks contrived and 67 × 30 × 35 = 70,350.00 still reproduces the PRD §16 headline); 67 Occupied, 13 Vacant. 67 active tenants with fictional Thai names and phone numbers, of which EXACTLY 54 carry a LINE binding — the number D-35's preview string quotes — and 13 deliberately do not, so D-30's ไม่มี LINE path is visible. Seeded bindings are placeholder IDs of the form Useed0000…{tenant_id}; they are never valid push targets, D-30's auto-unbind skips the Useed prefix, and LINE test mode defaults ON (D-34), so a stray send can never wipe the seeded state — the assertion is that after a full bulk approve against the seed the linked-tenant count is still 54. Rates effective from the first day of the earliest history period: 18.00 / 8.00 / 35.00; due day 5. History fully paid except the current period. One completed tenancy is seeded so the two riskiest flows are demonstrable: room 312 has an Inactive tenant whose final reading, final bill and Paid receipt sit in the previous period and a new Active tenant who moved in on the 1st of the current month, which exercises D-06, D-08 and D-14's gap note. Two users: admin/นิติบุคคล and staff/เจ้าหน้าที่, the admin password taken from SEED_ADMIN_PASSWORD (D-37). ALSO BINDING: the PRD §16 water (18,500) and electricity (62,500) totals are illustrative and NOT reproducible — 18,500 is not divisible by 18 and 62,500 is not divisible by 8 — and PRD §19's 35 ตร.ม. example row is illustrative in the same way; no document, mockup or test may treat any of the three as an expected value. Only the room counts (80/67/13) and the common area total (70,350) are reproduced.
decisions.rationale: The demo is the deliverable that gets graded, so its data is a product decision. Relative dates are the only way the graded demo shows a payable bill instead of an overdue one with a wrong receipt number; a uniform 30 ตร.ม. block makes the PRD's own headline Dashboard number come out exactly right without an examiner asking why vacant rooms are larger; and stating plainly which PRD figures are arithmetically impossible stops three documents being written against numbers the system can never produce.

decisions.question: What measurable targets and device targets do we commit to? (merges Q-U-20)
decisions.decision: Five committed numbers, each verifiable with a stopwatch against the D-44 seed: (1) a 67-room reading round completed on a phone in ≤ 15 minutes, measured from opening จดมิเตอร์ to the counter reading 67/67; (2) any list page renders in ≤ 2 seconds against the full seed (80 rooms × 12 periods ≈ 800 bills); (3) a single Approve & Send delivers the LINE bill within ≤ 30 seconds; (4) a 67-bill bulk approval COMMITS in ≤ 5 seconds and is fully delivered within ≤ 3 minutes, the two halves measured separately because they are two round trips (D-19); (5) Confirm Cash Payment to a printable receipt on screen in ≤ 5 seconds. Device targets: the phone surface (Login, จดมิเตอร์, and the reduced ภาพรวม) must work on Chrome for Android at 360 × 640 minimum with tap targets of at least 44 × 44 px and numeric keypads on every meter input; the Admin surface targets current Chrome and Edge on desktop at 1280 px and above and is not required to be usable below 768 px. Thai text renders in Noto Sans Thai with a system fallback on both. No uptime, concurrency or load-testing commitments are made.
decisions.rationale: PRD §3 objectives such as "ลดขั้นตอนการทำงาน" can never be passed or failed; these five numbers are what a capstone is actually judged on and each is measurable in a single sitting. Splitting target 4 matches how the feature is actually built and keeps a slow LINE API from failing an approval target it does not control.

assumptions: The apartment operates one reading round per calendar month, walked in the first few days of the month. If the real building reads mid-month the model still holds — only the month picker default changes.

PRD §12's sentence granting Confirm Cash Payment to เจ้าหน้าที่ contradicts §4 and is treated as a drafting error; §4 wins (D-36). This is the single place where a decision overrides literal PRD text, and it must be flagged in the document set.

PRD §16's ยอดค่าน้ำ 18,500 and ยอดค่าไฟ 62,500, and PRD §19's 35 ตร.ม. example room, are illustrative and not reproducible at the stated rates and seed; only the room counts and the 70,350 common area total are treated as reproducible (D-44).

PRD §28's calendar values (5 ก.ย. 2026, 3 ก.ย. 2026, REC-202609-000852) are documentation and mockup values. Every document uses them verbatim in examples; the live demo reproduces the arithmetic against relative dates, because due date, overdue display and receipt number are all functions of the run date (D-44).
'UtilityHub' at the top of the PRD is superseded by 'Juristic platform' at the bottom and by the existing template, repo and directory names; it is deleted rather than reconciled (D-01).

The juristic office is not VAT-registered for these charges and issues a plain ใบเสร็จรับเงิน; the tenant does not require a tax invoice (D-27). If a tax ID is unavailable the letterhead simply omits that line, which is why it is the one optional field on the receipt.

The receipt example REC-202609-000852 implies a continuous counter, since a 67-room building cannot reach 852 receipts within one month; the seed reproduces the 852 by starting the counter at an offset, which is one documented source of gaps in the sequence (D-27, D-44).
Water and electricity meters in the building are whole-unit mechanical meters with no fractional dial, so readings are integers (D-16). Switching to DECIMAL later is a single migration.

The team can register one LINE Official Account and enable the Messaging API. The free plan allows 500 push/multicast messages per month, which a 67-room building exceeds in normal operation; the demo stays inside it because test mode defaults ON and the graded run sends to at most three real accounts (D-34).
The office hands tenants a printed slip with the OA QR code and their one-time linking code; there is no other channel to distribute it (D-29).
Free-tier hosting sleeps and restarts; no scheduled work may live inside the Node process, no state may live in process memory, and staying awake requires its own 10-minute ping (D-32, D-37, D-43).

Approval of a period's bills happens within a few days of the reading round, which is what makes the MAX(due day, approval + 3 days) rule produce the office's usual due date rather than a shifted one (D-20).

Tenants pay in cash at the office during posted office hours; a tenant who cannot pay in full returns later — the counter never takes a part payment, and a refund after a voided payment is handed over in cash at the counter, never recorded as a system balance (D-24, D-25).
At most one person operates the counter at a time in practice; the concurrency guards in D-26 exist because a double click is certain, not because two cashiers are expected.
The team is 3-4 students over one semester with no dedicated QA, so every decision above was chosen to be implementable and testable by the same person who designed it.
Thai names, phone numbers and all seed content are fictional; no real tenant data enters the repository or the demo database.

Critic pass: all 41 findings were accepted and applied; none were declined. Ids were kept stable and the two new decisions were appended to their topic groups. The eleven structural consequences worth reading before any downstream document: (1) opening readings moved from a synthetic meter_readings row onto rooms.baseline_water / baseline_electric, which removes a unique-key collision that would have destroyed the first real reading (D-06, D-14); (2) the seed computes every date from CURDATE() and PRD §28's calendar values are documentation-only (D-44); (3) the one-live-payment rule is a stored generated column, because MySQL 8 has no partial index and a plain UNIQUE(bill_id) would make a corrected bill unpayable forever (D-26); (4) ending a tenancy is gated on a settled final bill instead of being a status flip, so a departing tenant's last month is never silently charged to the next tenant (D-08); (5) reverting a bill to Draft is restricted to a room's most recent bill, which is the only guard that keeps the previous_reading snapshot chain honest (D-22, D-12); (6) correcting a Paid bill returns the cash across the counter first — the system holds no refund, credit or balance (D-22, D-25); (7) notifications became one row per recipient with an attempt counter, covering announcements as well as bills, which is what makes retries, the manual resend and the monthly quota count all expressible (D-30, D-34, D-35); (8) bulk approval is two round trips — a fast commit then a drained queue — instead of one three-minute request (D-19, D-45); (9) rate resolution is keyed to the period, not the click, so a late second generation run cannot put two rates in one month (D-17); (10) the uptime ping is a separate 10-minute schedule, because the daily job is not a keep-alive and a cold-started webhook is how the LINE linking flow dies unnoticed (D-32, D-43); (11) the receipt sequence is stated once as unique and monotonic but NOT gapless, and the สำเนา mark is driven by a button rather than an unhookable browser print event (D-26, D-27).

Where reviewers disagreed I chose against the majority three times, each time for the cheaper option that still satisfies the demo and all 30 functions in PRD §18. (1) Overdue is derived, not a stored status written by a job (D-21) — a persisted status is wrong the moment free-tier hosting sleeps; the rule is now stated as a display rule so the Dashboard's deliberate aggregation over stored statuses is not a violation of it. (2) Full payment only, no partial payments (D-24) — this matches PRD §12's single button and removes overpayment entirely. (3) No period open/close state machine (D-11) — the bill status guard answers every question a period lock would have answered, and the word "closed" now appears nowhere; completeness is a derived line on Monthly Billing.

Two decisions are load-bearing for everything else and should be read first by every downstream document: D-11 (period = billing month) and D-21 (four display statuses, three stored, one shared helper).
